ticket.title: A task scoped to a repository with a configured chain was verified by the cargo-test fallback
ticket.description:
Found while verifying GB-337. The task is scoped to repo common with crate gaugeblock-contracts. The suite config HAS a chain keyed common, and the lookup order is crate, then repo, then default - so the repo key should have matched and run fmt/clippy/nextest/audit/docs. Instead the receipt says: no verification command configured for gaugeblock-contracts; falling back to cargo test, verifier storypole-verify:cargo-test-fallback.

So a ticket whose repository has a configured chain was certified by a weaker one. The receipt is honest about it - the warning exists and the verifier name differs - which is the good part and the reason this is a P2 rather than a P1: nothing is lying. But a weaker certification than the configuration promises is exactly the shape GB-272 and GB-316 were about, and it appeared for a ticket scoped to a repository that is in the list.

Worth checking: whether the repo lookup uses the task scope.repo value or derives a name from the checkout directory, whether the common entry is keyed exactly common, and whether the receipt should refuse rather than fall back when a repository key exists but did not match - falling back silently is how a member chain came to run harness commands once before (GB-316).
